headline: Architecture shapes how we live—buildings are frozen decisions about what matters
universal_truth: Environments shape behavior; the spaces we build become the lives we live
fun_facts: Cathedral ceilings make people think more abstractly; low ceilings promote focused thinking
The design of prisons, hospitals, and schools profoundly affects the people inside them
Ancient architects embedded astronomical alignments into structures—Stonehenge, pyramids, temples
discussion_questions: How do the buildings you inhabit affect how you feel?
What values are built into your home's design?
What would a building designed for human happiness look like?

hook.script: Buildings aren't just shelter—they're statements. A cathedral's towering space makes you feel small before God. A modern office's open plan says 'collaborate.' Architecture freezes decisions about values into structures we then live inside.

cliff.script: We think we live in buildings, but buildings also shape us. How does architecture actually influence human behavior and experience?

options.text: Spaces affect how we move, interact, feel, and think—we unconsciously adapt to our environments
options.response: Yes. High ceilings promote abstract thinking. Natural light improves mood. Hallway layouts determine who we encounter. We're shaped by spaces we barely notice.

options.text: Buildings provide practical functionality that we adapt to
options.response: Functionality matters, but the effects go much deeper into psychology...

fact1.title: Ceiling Effects
fact1.script: Studies show high ceilings encourage abstract, creative thinking—you feel freed. Low ceilings promote focused, detailed work—you feel contained. The space above your head changes what happens inside it.

fact2.title: Values in Stone
fact2.script: Every building embeds values. Prisons are designed to control. Hospitals are designed to heal. Churches to inspire awe. The priorities of designers become the experiences of inhabitants. Architecture is ethics made physical.

fact3.title: Lasting Influence
fact3.script: Buildings outlast their makers—often by centuries. The decisions of architects shape generations who never knew them. When you design a building, you're designing how future strangers will live. That's profound responsibility.

wisdom.script: Here's today's wisdom: Environments shape behavior. Architecture teaches that the spaces we build become the lives we live. Notice the buildings around you—they're silently influencing everything you do.

outro.script: That's Day 160—160 days of learning! Tomorrow, we'll explore what clothes communicate. Until then, notice how different spaces make you feel different ways.

growTrack.title: Space Awareness - Notice Your Environments
growTrack.activity: Move through different spaces today and notice how each affects you. A cramped room versus an open one. Natural light versus artificial. Quiet versus noisy. You're being shaped by architecture constantly. What would you change about the spaces you inhabit?
